text: I want a local tool for a neighborhood book swap. Volunteers record donated books and reserve them for neighbors. We have two volunteers, a $100 total budget, and four weeks. No accounts or payment processing for the MVP.
Start with a terminal app and a CSV file. The small scope makes a four-week delivery practical.
A browser interface could make it easier to show the catalog at the swap. I propose a local browser UI instead of a terminal app.
Before recommending an interface, I want to understand the volunteers' needs. QUESTION: Will volunteers share one computer, and are they comfortable using a terminal?
One shared laptop, offline at the venue. Both volunteers use terminals. Choose the terminal app; do not build the browser UI for this MVP.
CSV is easy to inspect but reservations can be corrupted by careless edits. SQLite could keep book and reservation updates consistent. QUESTION: Which storage approach should we use?
Use CSV initially. Store book title, author, and availability; a reservation records a neighbor's name and book.
I support CSV because volunteers can inspect it. First record donations, then list available books, then reserve a book. Run only one app instance at a time.
I am concerned about keeping neighbors' names indefinitely. A deletion policy needs to be decided; I propose deleting reservation names after collection.
I support a search command to find titles quickly. Barcode scanning could be a later convenience, but it has not been requested.

Change the storage choice to SQLite instead of CSV. Correct reservation updates matter more than editing a spreadsheet. Keep one local app instance and include title search. Barcode scanning is deferred until after the MVP.
I support SQLite for consistent reservations, provided we also test that a reserved book cannot be reserved again. I propose a backup command; the backup location is still unknown.
I revise my CSV recommendation: I now support SQLite because the user prioritizes reservation correctness. A donation-entry command and reservation command implement the agreed workflow.
Include a backup command, but leave the backup location undecided. I have not decided the name-retention policy either. Do not add cloud sync. Finish the plan with those questions open.
